hypothesis: If caterpillars and grubs feed and void excrement while chrysalises and other pupae do neither, a table that records feeding or excretion for both a larval stage and a pupal stage of a butterfly, bee or wasp will show intake or frass in larvae and none in pupae.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. A qualifying file has a stage variable that separates larva/caterpillar/grub from pupa/chrysalis, and a feeding or excretion variable (intake, feeding, frass, feces, excretion, defecation). Pass only if at least one qualifying file shows larval rows with feeding or excretion greater than zero and pupal rows with both feeding and excretion equal to zero, and no pupal row with either quantity greater than zero. Meconium or adult emergence output is not pupal excretion and is ignored if the stage is adult.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Any pupal row with feeding or excretion greater than zero refutes the pupal clause. Larval rows all at zero would refute the larval clause. If no planned file has both the stage contrast and a feeding or excretion variable, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable. Values in a non-qualifying file are not analysed.
interpretation: The claim contrasts larval feeding and defecation with a pupa that does neither, for butterflies and for other insects that pupate, named as bees and wasps. Only a table that actually crosses stage with intake or excretion can test it. Pupal mass, development time and adult feeding do not.

test_contract.expected_observation: Larvae have positive feeding or excretion and pupae have zero of both, in the same table.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: A pupa with positive feeding or positive excretion, or larvae that neither feed nor excrete.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Open downloadable tables of insects that name larval and pupal stages and record intake or excretion. Narrative species accounts are not admissible. Files that lack those variables are recorded as inspected and then dropped.
test_contract.inference_method: Column-header screen first. If no file qualifies, stop with data-unavailable and do not use body values. If a file qualifies, compare larval versus pupal values of the feeding and excretion columns against zero.

caveats: Dataset descriptions and column lists were read to choose these two Dryad packages. A search snippet also showed six larval rows of an R teaching table; that table is not planned and those values are not used.
Bees and wasps are inside the claim. A butterfly-only table would not by itself cover them; the criterion above still applies to whatever qualifying rows exist.
method: Downloaded the landing pages of the two pre-registered Dryad packages. Each spreadsheet URL failed, so no header row was read and no body value was used. The verdict is data-unavailable.
